summary: PulseGuard v0.6.30 fixes a Windows PowerShell 5.1 generic-collection type-binding crash that could stop FIX & OPTIMIZE while building the driver-update audit, and adds a preflight regression test so this exact failure is caught before maintenance begins.

sections.heading: FIX & OPTIMIZE driver-audit crash fixed
sections.detail: The driver-update audit no longer passes a generic List[object] through Windows PowerShell 5.1 array-subexpression counting. The code now counts ICollection/IEnumerable values safely and resolves UpdatedCount independently, preventing the System.ArgumentException: Argument types do not match failure seen while exporting the maintenance report.

sections.heading: Regression test added to safety preflight
sections.detail: Preflight now constructs and counts a real generic List[object] and runs a mock driver-update audit. If Windows PowerShell cannot safely process that exact data shape, FIX & OPTIMIZE is blocked before any maintenance action starts instead of failing later in the workflow.

sections.heading: Driver audit fallback hardened
sections.detail: When a driver engine result omits or returns an unusable UpdatedCount value, PulseGuard now falls back to the number of verified collected update rows without unsafe nested expression evaluation. Driver audit items are converted to a plain object array before report serialization.

sections.heading: All recent repair and updater fixes retained
sections.detail: v0.6.30 retains the v0.6.29 GitHub release validation, v0.6.28 incomplete-install recovery, v0.6.27 SFC/WHEA/WinGet/driver-audit fixes, and the guarded sppsvc repair lane from v0.6.26.
